questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{3}{{x}^{4}},\,x>1
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{3}{2},$ compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}+2X-1].$

*Hint: You may assume that $\text{E}[aX+bY]=a\text{E}[X]+b\text{E}[Y]$ for any random variables $X$ and $Y$ and constants $a$ and $b.$*
questions.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the hint and the properties of expected value:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}+2X-1] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]+2\text{E}[X]-\text{E}[1] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]+2\text{E}[X]-1\end{aligned}
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We already know $\text{E}[X].$ So, we compute the second raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{3}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{a}\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{(-\frac{3}{x})|}_{1}^{a} \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }(3-\frac{3}{a}) \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\text{E}[X]=\frac{3}{2}$ and $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]=3$ into the simplified expression, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}+2X-1] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]+2\text{E}[X]-1 \\  & =3+2\cdot \frac{3}{2}-1 \\  & =3+3-1 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{x},\,1<x<e
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=e-1,$ compute $\text{E}[2{X}^{2}-X].$

*Hint: You may assume that $\text{E}[aX+bY]=a\text{E}[X]+b\text{E}[Y]$ for any random variables $X$ and $Y$ and constants $a$ and $b.$*
questions.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the hint and the properties of expected value:

$$
\text{E}[2{X}^{2}-X]=2\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We already know $\text{E}[X].$ So, we compute the second raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\,|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\text{E}[X]=e-1$ and $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]=\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{2}$ into the simplified expression, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2{X}^{2}-X] & =2\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X] \\  & =2\cdot \frac{{e}^{2}-1}{2}-(e-1) \\  & ={e}^{2}-1-e+1 \\  & ={e}^{2}-e.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{2},\,1<x<3
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=2,$ compute $\text{E}[5X-3{X}^{2}].$

*Hint: You may assume that $\text{E}[aX+bY]=a\text{E}[X]+b\text{E}[Y]$ for any random variables $X$ and $Y$ and constants $a$ and $b.$*
questions.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the hint and the properties of expected value:

$$
\text{E}[5X-3{X}^{2}]=5\text{E}[X]-3\text{E}[{X}^{2}]
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We already know $\text{E}[X].$ So, we compute the second raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}\,|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{13}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\text{E}[X]=2$ and $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]=\frac{13}{3}$ into the simplified expression, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[5X-3{X}^{2}] & =5\text{E}[X]-3\text{E}[{X}^{2}] \\  & =5\cdot 2-3\cdot \frac{13}{3} \\  & =10-13 \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{4}(1-x),\,-2\le x\le 0.
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{3}].$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the third raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{3}] & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{x}^{3}\cdot \frac{1}{4}(1-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{-2}^{0}({x}^{3}-{x}^{4})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}-\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}){|}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(0-[4+\frac{32}{5}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(-\frac{52}{5}) \\  & =-\frac{13}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{2x},\,1\le x\le {e}^{2}.
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{4}].$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the fourth raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{4}] & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}{x}^{4}\cdot \frac{1}{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\,{x}^{4}\,{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}({e}^{8}-1) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{8}-1}{8}\end{aligned}
$$
